brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: Four level-1 bases (piece:0,0,1 to 3,0,1) each with a full-depth drained PVC-bore bin (bin:*~hex-bin-full-drain-pvc), all filled with soil and planted (prop:1-4).

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell
requirements.evidence: Irrigation run run:run-1 passes in a straight line through all four level-0 bases (0,0 to 3,0), with a vertical riser (riser:*,0,0) in every cell rising into the PVC bore of the planter bin directly above, so the run feeds all four cells. Note the configurator checks fit only; actual waterproofing/water delivery depends on the printed material and assembly, which it cannot verify.

finish.summary: Built a four-cell planter in a row: an irrigation pipe runs through the four ground-level bases, a riser in each cell rises into the PVC bore of a drained planter bin stacked above, and all four bins are filled with soil and planted. Open faces capped, joints locked, check_build clear with no mesh clash.

lines.label: Bin, full depth, drained, PVC bore
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
